newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear resumes some output at strikebound plants.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear resumes some output at strikebound plants.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. resumed limited production at nine strikebound plants Monday in an effort to keep tire supplies flowing to automakers as negotiators attempted to resolve the dispute.
"We are continuing to produce. We cannot maintain it at the rate we would be able to if we had a full complement of workers," said Goodyear spokesman John Perduyn.
About 13,000 members of the United Steelworkers of America walked off their jobs just after midnight Sunday in the first strike in 21 years at the largest U.S. tiremaker.
Goodyear was chosen as the union's negotiating target to set the industry pattern for a new three-year labor contract, and two months of negotiations failed to produce an agreement.
Detroit's Big Three automakers Monday were assessing their inventories of Goodyear products and whether they needed to make arrangements with other manufacturers.
"We don't expect to have any immediate impact because we have a reasonable supply of Goodyear products on hand," said General Motors Corp. spokesman Daniel Jankowski.

GM, the world's largest automaker, currently buys about 30 percent of the tires used in its North American vehicles from Goodyear, but it could quickly shift to other manufacturers in order to keep assembly lines rolling, Jankowski said.

Ford Motor Co. spokeswoman Cheryl Eberwein said the company has not yet been affected by the strike, but will assess the situation day by day. She added that Ford buys a number of other rubber products from Goodyear, including hoses and engine mounts.

Chrysler Corp said it had enough tires to keep most of its still-operating plants running for about three weeks. The automaker has idled six assembly plants in the United States, Canada and Mexico because of a separate dispute at its Mound Road engine plant in Detroit.

Talks between Goodyear and the United Steelworkers resumed Monday morning in Cincinnati with only a portion of the full negotiating committees taking part. The talks were adjourned Monday night and were slated to resume Tuesday morning.
"We just know that they're continuing to talk, Perduyn said.
The workers struck Goodyear plants in Akron, Marysville, and St. Marys, Ohio; Gadsden, Ala.; Lincoln, Neb.; Topeka, Kan.; Danville, Va.; Union City, Tenn.; and Sun Prairie, Wis.
Issues in dispute include job security, contracting out work, contract revisions and certain partnership arrangements, said the union.
The strike was the first to hit Goodyear since a 140-day-long work stoppage that paralyzed the tire industry in 1976.
Goodyear employs 91,000 people at dozens of plants around the world. It stock fell 25 cents to $52 Monday in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
